subject: Lightweight OTEL shim compatibility pilot — Observify / Datadog / Grafana
messages:
From: Observify Integrations <partner@observify.io>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot proposal — lightweight OTEL shim for inference edge SDKs

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the intro call last week — the Observify team is excited about a small pilot to validate a lightweight OpenTelemetry (OTEL) shim that surfaces runtime metrics and traces from Redwood's inference sidecar and embedded SDKs. Our goal is to make the shim low footprint (<= 500KB binary delta), TLS-ready, and compatible with OTLP/gRPC and HTTP exporters (Datadog/Grafana).

We sketched a 2-week technical spike to: 
- implement a minimal shim that translates Redwood runtime telemetry APIs -> OTLP
- verify end-to-end export to Datadog and to a Grafana Tempo/OTLP ingestion endpoint
- measure CPU/memory overhead on a 4GB-instance inference workload

Attached is a short spec (shim-spec-v0.1.pdf) and a resource estimate. Would Redwood be willing to run the spike in a sandbox Dedicated pool? We can co-fund the pilot hours and publish a joint short writeup afterwards.

Proposed kickoff: Mon 2027-11-15 (2 week window)
Key asks from Redwood: test harness access + contact for any build/runtime questions.

Cheers,
Maya Park
Head of Integrations, Observify
partner@observify.io

Attachment: shim-spec-v0.1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
Attachment: resource-estimate.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Observify Integrations <partner@observify.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal — lightweight OTEL shim for inference edge SDKs

Maya — thanks, this looks promising.

We can support a 2-week spike in a sandbox Dedicated pool. Ben, Laura — looping you in for capacity and partner ops. Quick answers:
- Sandbox access: yes, we can provision a small Dedicated slice with RBAC for Observify.
- Test harness: we have a lightweight infer-runner that reproduces CPU/latency profiles; Ben will share details.
- Legal/PS: we'll draft a short SOW (two week engagement, mutual writeup).

I can kickoff on 11/15. Observify: can you confirm the top 3 telemetry signals you need (e.g., token_latency_ms, kvcache_hits, model_load_time) and whether you prefer OTLP/gRPC first or HTTP?

Thanks — looking forward.

— Jasmine Liu
Principal Partner Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal — lightweight OTEL shim for inference edge SDKs

Jasmine / Laura — quick ops note before we confirm:
- Capacity: Sandbox Dedicated slice ok; estimated 120 GPU-hours across two weeks per the resource-estimate.xlsx (attached). I'll ask infra to reserve a T4-equivalent pool.
- Security: Observify will need a service account token. We should require a timebound key (7-14 days) and restrict it to the sandbox cluster.
- Metrics whitelist: propose we start with these signals: token_generation_ms (p50/p95), kvcache_hit_ratio, queue_length, and model_load_duration_ms. That should be minimal and useful for dashboards.

Laura — can you own the SOW draft and put a couple of standard clauses for co-marketing? I'll also add a brief procurement note to finance.

Attachment: redwood-pilot-sow-draft.docx

Ben Carter
Partner Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Observify Integrations <partner@observify.io>, Datadog PM <pm@datadog.com>, Grafana Integrations <integrations@grafana.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal — lightweight OTEL shim for inference edge SDKs

Folks — kickoff confirmed for tomorrow (2027-11-16) morning. Short agenda and asks below.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m introductions and success criteria (Observify + Redwood + Datadog/Grafana)
- 10m shim design walkthrough (Observify) — transport, batching, TLS expectations
- 10m test plan and metrics to validate overhead (Redwood/Ben)
- 5m next steps (SOW signature, sandbox credentials, onboarding doc links)

Asks from vendors:
- Datadog: will you confirm recommended receiver config for OTLP/gRPC for short-lived sandbox keys and whether metrics->APM mapping needs any special tags?
- Grafana: please confirm Tempo/OTLP ingestion endpoint and recommended traceID header expectations so Observify can map tracing spans.

Observify — please upload the final shim binary prototype and a small test harness to the Jira ticket: https://jira.redwood/OBS-44 before tomorrow's call. We'll keep the call focused and then split into breakout sessions if needed.

I'll send calendar invites for 11/16 09:00 PT. Thanks everyone — excited to move fast on a low-friction integration that makes Redwood runtime telemetry consumable by common observability stacks.

— Jasmine
Principal Partner Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
